| [CASE-307](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-307.md) | Revision rates of claims with inbound edges | [LEAD-199](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-199.md)'s count, as it specified. Population: the 859 claim files on staging, followed through renames and formerly: fields, over the record's whole history (2026-10-07 to 2026-11-22, about 46 days). A revision is substantive if it changes the title, role, warrant, defeated_if or the body outside dated notes, after normalising away link markup, directives, cited codes and citation-only parentheses; schema backfills and bot commits are excluded. Exposure: the replayed count of other entries naming the claim in rests_on or grounds. Result, at matched age (Mantel-Haenszel by age bin): claims with any inbound edge are revised 1.47 times as often as claims with none (95% interval 1.22 to 1.77; 1.45 stratified by age and calendar week; 1.62 by risk-set matching over seven days), and title and status changes rise too. The raw fall from before to after the first edge (ratio 0.58) is the filing-day burst: it vanishes when each claim's first day is dropped (1.04). The 6+ group has 4 to 7 events and an interval including 1. Classifier precision by hand-check: about 0.7 by intent, 0.9 by the letter. 148 of the 303 revisions after a first edge fall within a day of it, so edges and revisions come in the same working sessions. | Proposed |
